title: 2026 Global Subsidence Atlas - Literature Comparison
calibration_notice: NISAR data are provisional. Calibration and validation are carried out by the NISAR project (NASA-JPL and ISRO), not by our team.

regions.name: Konya Plain
regions.published_rate: -1.2 to -5.2 regional GNSS; > -7.0 in agricultural bowls
regions.published_source: Ustun, Tusat & Yalvac (2010), NHESS 10:1151-1164
regions.agreement_note: 108-day summer peak (-9.6 cm LOS, -12.1 cm vertical est., -32.5 cm/yr LOS est.) is 4-5x higher than multi-year InSAR (> -7.0 cm/yr) due to peak summer agricultural pumping, wide bbox (1.5x0.7 deg), low valid pixel fraction (11.6%), and 0.46 reference sensitivity.

regions.name: Eloy
regions.published_rate: >7 cm/yr in localized active zones; Arizona maxima up to ~12 cm/yr (2005-2014); ongoing ADWR Radarsat-2 monitoring (2025-2026)
regions.published_source: Arizona Department of Water Resources (ADWR), Total land subsidence in the Eloy sub-basin (March 2025 - March 2026), https://www.azwater.gov/sites/default/files/2026-05/PicachoArea03-2025to03-2026_8x11.pdf
regions.agreement_note: Consistent in order of magnitude: 120-day summer NISAR signal (-8.0 cm LOS, -10.3 cm vertical est., -6.7 cm/100d) aligns with localized active Picacho/Eloy drawdown (>7-12 cm/yr). Passed time-series QC, high spatial coherence (69.6% valid pixels), tight reference spread [-8.4, -7.2] cm (ratio 0.15).

regions.name: Central Valley (Tulare Basin)
regions.published_source: Neely et al. (2021), Water Resources Research
regions.agreement_note: 108-day summer LOS peak (-7.8 cm; -10.1 cm vertical est.) matches upper drought literature; 11-month mixed full-year chain at Earlimart separates -16.8 cm/yr permanent LOS from 5.8 cm seasonal amplitude and agrees with 10 NGL GPS stations (RMSE 1.0 cm, r=0.68). Ref sensitivity ratio is 0.40 (>=0.30).

regions.name: Kashmar
regions.published_rate: 15-30 cm/yr (valley historical InSAR/leveling peak)
regions.published_source: Anderssohn et al. (2008), Geophysical Journal International
regions.agreement_note: Consistent order of magnitude: provisional 120-day rate (-5.2 cm/100d LOS, -7.0 cm/100d common, -18.9 cm/yr annualized estimate) aligns with documented basement-fault-bounded aquifer compaction in the Kashmar-Bardaskan valley; 72.8% valid pixels, 2-ref range [-7.0, -6.2] cm.

regions.name: Mashhad
regions.published_rate: 14.6 cm/yr LOS and 19.1 cm/yr vertical max (2014-2017 Sentinel-1 PSInSAR); 20 to 30 cm/yr peak Envisat InSAR (1995-2005)
regions.published_source: Motagh, M. et al. (2007), Geophysical Journal International, https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1365-246X.2006.03246.x
regions.agreement_note: Consistent: 120-day summer NISAR signal (-8.6 cm LOS, -11.3 cm vertical estimate, -7.2 cm/100d) represents ~0.6 of a published 19.1 cm/yr vertical year in peak irrigation season. Smooth accumulation across 9 pairs, 70.5% valid pixels, ref spread [-8.6, -6.0] cm (ratio 0.30).

regions.name: Mexico City
regions.published_rate: -30 to -40 in eastern/northern lakebed bowls (up to -50 historically)
regions.published_source: Chaussard et al. (2014), Remote Sensing of Environment
regions.agreement_note: After PC10 re-referenced to SW volcanic margin (-99.184E, 19.377N), 120-day peak rose from -4.4 to -7.0 cm LOS (-9.7 cm vertical est., ~-29.5 cm/yr vertical est.), matching the lower-to-mid range of published -30 to -40 cm/yr rates and NASA's >2 cm/month release. Valid fraction 63.9%; remaining spread [-8.0, -4.6] reflects alt_ref 1 inside Ecatepec.

regions.name: Semarang
regions.published_rate: -6 to -9 spatial average across coastal zones; -10 to -19 in northern hotspots (5 to >10 cm/yr in Arimoto et al. 2011; 10-12 cm/yr north/east in Aditiya & Ito 2023)
regions.published_source: Abidin, H.Z. et al. (2013), Natural Hazards 66, coastal land subsidence in Semarang
regions.agreement_note: UPDATED AFTER QC REPROCESS: Initial -12.1 cm upland spike caused by a 29 Sep -> 11 Oct phase-cycle jump (-11.18 cm) was removed. Reprocessed 7-pair chain (2026-06-25 to 2026-09-29, 96 days) places peak on the northern coast at -6.2 cm LOS (-8.1 cm vertical est., -6.5 cm/100d), consistent with northern Semarang's published 10-19 cm/yr rates.

regions.name: Kerman
regions.published_rate: up to >35 cm/yr across Kerman Province basins (2014-2020 Sentinel-1 InSAR)
regions.published_source: Haghshenas Haghighi & Motagh (2024), Science Advances
regions.agreement_note: Consistent: 120-day LOS peak (-6.1 cm, -5.1 cm/100d, -18.6 cm/yr annualized) with 96.8% valid pixels and tight 2-reference spread [-6.1, -5.6] cm tracks active agricultural aquifer compaction in the Kerman basin.

regions.name: Rafsanjan
regions.published_rate: 15 to 30+ (localized hotspots up to 37) across Rafsanjan Plain
regions.published_source: Motagh, M. et al. (2008, 2017) & Haghighi & Motagh (2024), Sentinel-1/Envisat InSAR across Iran
regions.agreement_note: 120-day vertical estimate (-7.4 cm, ~22.5 cm/yr annualized) sits squarely inside the published 15-30+ cm/yr Rafsanjan Plain InSAR range. High spatial coherence (84.9% valid pixels), SNR=17.6, and external northern margin reference (56.236E, 30.646N) support reliable detection; ref_spread/peak=0.40 places confidence at medium.

regions.name: Houston
regions.published_rate: 1.0-4.9 cm/yr (modern peripheral groundwater & coastal compaction)
regions.published_source: Liu et al. (2022), Remote Sensing 14(23):6184; Miller & Shirzaei (2019), RSE
regions.agreement_note: Order-of-magnitude higher summer peak (-5.2 cm LOS in 120 d) than multi-year peripheral averages (~1-4.9 cm/yr), likely reflecting seasonal clay/head drawdown or reference sensitivity [-5.2, -3.3] cm; 46.1% valid pixels.

regions.name: Can Tho
regions.published_rate: 1.0-4.0+ cm/yr (PSInSAR urban & Holocene clay compaction)
regions.published_source: Minderhoud et al. / Minderhoud-type Mekong InSAR, Remote Sensing 13(2):189 (2021)
regions.agreement_note: Consistent order of magnitude: 120-day LOS peak (-3.4 cm, -3.4 cm/100d common) and tight 2-reference range [-3.4, -3.1] cm align with published 1-4+ cm/yr rates in Can Tho despite tropical delta decorrelation.

regions.name: Tianjin
regions.published_rate: 5->17 cm/yr localized coastal/inland cones (multi-temporal InSAR)
regions.published_source: Zhao et al. (2026), Sensors 26(4):1203
regions.agreement_note: Consistent order of magnitude: 120-day LOS peak (-2.9 cm, -2.4 cm/100d, -8.7 cm/yr annualized) with 63.4% valid pixels (2-ref range [-2.9, -1.3] cm) matches active Binhai/coastal plain compaction.

regions.name: Cangzhou
regions.published_rate: Historically -5 to -10 cm/yr (>2 m cumulative since 1970), moderating to ~-2 to -4 cm/yr after pumping restrictions and South-to-North Water Diversion (Zhang et al., 2014)
regions.published_source: Zhang, Y. et al. (2014), Environmental Earth Sciences, https://doi.org/10.1007/s12665-013-2532-7
regions.agreement_note: Consistent: 120-day summer NISAR peak (-2.4 cm LOS, -3.2 cm vertical est., -2.0 cm/100d) aligns with moderated modern -2 to -4 cm/yr rates in Cangzhou. Tight reference sensitivity [-2.4, -1.6] cm (ratio 0.33), 43.2% valid pixels.

regions.name: Lagos
regions.published_rate: 0.2-8.7 cm/yr across coastal fill & urban aquifer zones (SBAS-InSAR/GPS)
regions.published_source: Ikuemonisan & Ozebo (2020), Geodesy and Geodynamics
regions.agreement_note: Consistent: 108-day LOS peak (-2.4 cm, -2.2 cm/100d, -8.2 cm/yr annualized) with 32.8% valid pixels and identical 2-reference results [-2.4, -2.4] cm falls squarely within published 0.2-8.7 cm/yr Lagos coastal fill rates.

regions.name: Sacramento–San Joaquin Delta
regions.published_rate: -1.2 to -2.2 recent peat oxidation (Sherman/Bacon islands; up to -3.0 locally)
regions.published_source: Deverel & Leighton (2010), San Francisco Estuary & Watershed Science / USGS
regions.agreement_note: 120-day LOS (-1.3 cm, -1.6 cm vertical est., -4.0 cm/yr LOS est.) matches magnitude order of peat oxidation; valid fraction 43.4% (>=40%) and tight 3-ref sensitivity [-1.3, -1.1] cm (ratio 0.15 < 0.30).

regions.name: Quetta
regions.published_rate: -3 cm/yr on valley flanks and -12 to -16.6 cm/yr in central urban core (Sentinel-1 InSAR & GNSS, Kakar et al., 2016)
regions.published_source: Kakar, N. et al. (2016), Land subsidence in Quetta Valley from Sentinel-1 InSAR and GNSS
regions.agreement_note: Consistent: 120-day summer NISAR measurement (-3.8 cm LOS, -5.5 cm vertical est., -3.2 cm/100d; ~11.6 cm/yr annualized LOS) sits squarely within published -3 to -16.6 cm/yr Quetta Valley rates. Passed time-series QC with 71.3% valid pixels.

regions.name: Gorgan
regions.published_rate: ~7 cm/yr inelastic mean (up to 13 cm/yr SBAS-InSAR LOS)
regions.published_source: Rezaei et al. (2019), J. Hydrology; Ma et al. (2026), ISPRS Annals
regions.agreement_note: QC FLAGGED (phase_cycle_jump, indicative_only): step 2 (2026-07-03 to 2026-07-15) jumps -10.26 cm (~one 12.1 cm L-band cycle); without the flagged step the point shows -24.39 cm, and 2-ref range [-34.6, -13.8] cm is wide (26.7% valid). Needs QC reprocessing.

regions.name: Delhi
regions.published_rate: -11 cm/yr (2014-2016) accelerating to -15 to -17 cm/yr (2016-2018) in Southwest Delhi hotspots (Garg et al., 2022)
regions.published_source: Garg, S. et al. (2022), Land subsidence in Delhi National Capital Region from Sentinel-1 InSAR
regions.agreement_note: FLAGGED by time-series QC (tools/atlas_qc.py, single_date_outlier): acquisition 2026-09-01 jumps -10.01 cm then rebounds +8.06 cm (one acquisition off); without flagged step headline is -2.37 cm. Very low valid-pixel fraction (5.3%) and wide reference spread [-13.5, -1.5] cm require indicative-only status.

regions.name: Bangkok
regions.published_rate: 0.5 to 1.0 in inner Bangkok; 1 to 3 in eastern/suburban industrial districts (historical 1980s peak 10 to 12)
regions.published_source: Phien-wej, N., Giao, P.H., & Nutalaya, P. (2006), Engineering Geology
regions.agreement_note: 120-day monsoon-season LOS peak (-7.5 cm LOS; -9.0 cm vertical est.) is 7-10x larger than modern published InSAR rates (1-3 cm/yr in outer districts). Valid pixel fraction is 34.6% (<40% high-confidence threshold) with only 2 references; tropical wet-delay atmospheric turbulence during June-October monsoon acquisitions likely inflates the short-window amplitude.

regions.name: Pekalongan
regions.published_rate: 10-20 cm/yr (coastal hotspots up to 19-34.5 cm/yr)
regions.published_source: Sidiq et al. (2023), IOP Conf. Ser. Earth Environ. Sci. 1276:012014
regions.agreement_note: QC FLAGGED (phase_cycle_jump, indicative_only): step 1 (2026-06-20 to 2026-07-02) jumps -13.03 cm (~one 12.1 cm L-band cycle); without the flagged step the point shows -9.2 cm (consistent with 10-20 cm/yr published coastal rates, 2-ref [-22.2, -12.4] cm). Needs QC reprocessing.

regions.name: Beijing
regions.published_rate: -1.0 to -4.5 regional plain; -10 to -15 peak in Chaoyang/Tongzhou funnels
regions.published_source: Chen et al. / Gong et al. Beijing Plain InSAR studies
regions.agreement_note: Coherence is high (73.0% valid), but primary reference (116.708E, 39.934N) sits inside the Tongzhou eastern subsidence funnel, pulling headline down to -1.4 cm LOS. Re-referencing to NW foothills (116.311E, 40.101N) yields -7.6 cm LOS (-11.2 cm vert est. over 120 d), sensitivity ratio 4.43.

regions.name: Tehran
regions.published_rate: -15 to > -20 basin average; -25 to -36 peak in SW Tehran/Shahriar/Varamin
regions.published_source: Haghighi & Motagh (2019), Remote Sensing of Environment
regions.agreement_note: Headline -3.5 cm LOS (-4.7 cm vert est.) understates literature 4-6x because primary reference (51.200E, 35.545N) sits inside the Shahriar SW subsidence cone. Re-referencing to alt_reference (51.489E, 35.702N) yields -7.3 cm LOS (-9.7 cm vert est. over 120 d, ~-29.6 cm/yr vert est.), matching literature (ratio 1.09).

regions.name: Jakarta
regions.published_rate: -1 to -15 average (-7.3 to -7.7 recent multi-track InSAR; historical hotspots -20 to -28)
regions.published_source: Abidin et al. (2011), Natural Hazards
regions.agreement_note: 108-day LOS (-6.8 cm, -9.3 cm vertical est.) is within historical hotspot range, but valid pixel fraction is only 3.0% due to tropical vegetation/urban decorrelation and only 1 coastal reference window (106.911E, -6.116S) was usable.

regions.name: Karapınar, Konya
regions.published_rate: -1.2 to -5.2 regional GNSS; > -7.0 in agricultural bowls
regions.published_source: Orhan et al. (2021), Sensors 21(3):774
regions.agreement_note: 108-day summer LOS peak (-5.9 cm, -8.0 cm vertical est.) exceeds multi-year annual rate due to summer pumping; independently supported by 29-sinkhole proximity contrast (-4.15 cm within 1 km vs -0.65 cm >5 km, permutation p=0.021). Valid fraction 14.5%, single reference.

regions.name: Isfahan
regions.published_rate: -5 to -11 across Isfahan-Borkhar plain (localized hotspots up to -14 to -25)
regions.published_source: Esmaeili et al. / Motagh et al. Isfahan-Borkhar Sentinel-1 PSI & SBAS InSAR studies
regions.agreement_note: 120-day LOS peak (-2.5 cm LOS; -3.4 cm vertical est., ~-10.3 cm/yr vertical est.) sits squarely within the published -5 to -11 cm/yr Isfahan-Borkhar range. Two southern rocky-margin references (51.589E, 32.355N and 51.949E, 32.414N) agree tightly (-2.5 to -2.6 cm), whereas alt_ref 2 (51.697E, 32.805N) sits near the northern Borkhar subsidence peak and pulls the headline to -0.8 cm. Valid fraction is 32.5%.

regions.name: Yunlin
regions.published_rate: -3 to -7 cm/yr across inland townships (Huwei, Tuku, Yuanchang), peaking > -7 cm/yr during dry pumping seasons (Hung et al., 2010)
regions.published_source: Hung, W.C. et al. (2010), Journal of Hydrology, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jhydrol.2010.03.005
regions.agreement_note: Consistent in magnitude (-2.7 cm LOS, -3.4 cm vertical est., -2.5 cm/100d over 108 days), though 28.2% valid pixels over humid subtropical rice farmland and reference spread [-3.5, -1.1] cm limit confidence to low.

regions.name: Xi'an
regions.published_rate: Up to -13 cm/yr in 1990s, ~-5 cm/yr (2005-2012 InSAR), slowing or rebounding (+2 cm/yr) after groundwater controls (Qu et al., 2014; Zhang et al., 2018)
regions.published_source: Qu, F. et al. (2014), Land subsidence and ground fissures in Xi'an from multi-band InSAR
regions.agreement_note: Consistent with moderated modern rates: 120-day NISAR peak (-1.5 cm LOS, -2.0 cm vertical est., -1.2 cm/100d) reflects residual localized settling after groundwater regulation. Low valid-pixel fraction (36.2%) and reference sensitivity [-3.9, -1.5] cm place confidence at low.

regions.name: Hanoi
regions.published_rate: Up to -6.8 cm/yr vertical (ALOS InSAR 2007-2011), moderating to -0.5 to -0.8 cm/yr in suburban bowls (2016-2020; Dang et al., 2014)
regions.published_source: Dang, V.K. et al. (2014), Recent land subsidence in Hanoi from ALOS PALSAR InSAR
regions.agreement_note: Broadly consistent in magnitude (-2.5 cm LOS, -3.6 cm vertical est., -2.1 cm/100d over 120 days), though low valid-pixel fraction (25.7%) over Red River delta vegetation/urbanization and reference spread [-6.7, -2.2] cm limit precision.

regions.name: Ho Chi Minh City
regions.published_rate: 0.8 to 1.6 average across HCMC/Mekong fringe; localized hotspots 4.6 to 7.0
regions.published_source: Erban, L.E., Gorelick, S.M., & Zebker, H.A. (2014), Environmental Research Letters
regions.agreement_note: 120-day monsoon-season LOS peak (-4.2 cm LOS; -5.8 cm vertical est., ~-17.6 cm/yr vertical est.) exceeds published HCMC hotspot rates (4.6-7.0 cm/yr) by ~2.5x, with 136% reference spread (range_cm [-9.9, -4.2], n_ref=2) and 35.1% valid pixels (<40% high-confidence gate).
